output_json.diff_review: Reviewed patch_only.diff directly. Core fix: FileUtils.java gains directoryPathTraversal(String dirPath) which splits on "/" and rejects any trimmed segment equal to ".." or any backslash/null input. ResourcesServiceImpl.java calls this new check immediately after the existing name/fileSuffix directoryTraversal checks and before fullName is built, at exactly the three sites the exploiter/alert flagged: createDirectory (~line 140), createResource (~line 220), onlineCreateResource (~line 968) — each returning Status.VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED on rejection, matching the existing convention for the sibling name-validation failure. Confirmed via source inspection that updateResource never accepts a raw currentDir (it derives the parent from resource.getFullName(), already validated at creation time) and separately validates the new leaf `name` through verifyFile()'s FileUtils.directoryTraversal(name) call before the HDFS copy sink — so the fix's root-cause reasoning holds and no sink is left unguarded. Three matching unit tests added to ResourcesServiceTest (createDirectory/createResource/onlineCreateResource with a malicious currentDir, asserting VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED and that resourcesMapper.insert is never invoked) plus a focused FileUtilsTest.testDirectoryPathTraversal covering legitimate paths, various ".." placements including the exact POV payload, and backslash/null inputs. No POV files were touched by patch_only.diff. One incidental, non-security artifact: a new file test/testFile.txt (garbage placeholder content) was added — this is a pre-existing fixture required by an unrelated, already-present FileUtilsTest method (line 84 references "test/testFile.txt") that was apparently untracked in the repo; it is not part of the vulnerability fix, does not change behavior, and is not a security concern, just repo hygiene noise.
issues: Minor/non-blocking: patch_only.diff includes an incidental new file test/testFile.txt with placeholder garbage content, which is a fixture required by a pre-existing (unmodified) FileUtilsTest method rather than part of the security fix itself — repo hygiene noise, not a security or correctness concern.

Pre-existing gap outside this alert's scope (not introduced or worsened by this patch): FileUtils.directoryPathTraversal only rejects an exact '..' segment after trim; it would not catch encoded traversal variants (e.g. '%2e%2e') if such encoding ever survived to this layer un-decoded, though this matches the existing directoryTraversal(name) check's same limitation and is consistent with how DolphinScheduler already handles this class of input.
output_json.pov_result: Reran via the docker wrapper logs provided: pov_before_patch (unpatched worktree) exits 0 with "OK (1 test)", confirming the malicious currentDir ("/pov/../../../../../../../../tmp/dolphin_pwn") reaches resourcesMapper.insert and HadoopUtils.getHdfsFileName with the un-sanitized traversal path, normalizing outside the tenant root. pov_after_patch (patched worktree, same unmodified POV file) exits 1: createDirectory now returns "The file name verify failed" (Status.VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED) and the test's own assertion (expecting resourcesMapper.insert to have been invoked so it can capture/verify the tainted fullName) fails because insert was never called — i.e., the exploit path is blocked before any DB write or HDFS call, which is the correct/expected outcome for a fix (POV designed to succeed only when vulnerable). This is consistent behavior, not POV tampering — patch_only.diff confirms the POV harness file itself was not modified.
output_json.regression_result: Full reactor build (mvn -DskipTests package) succeeds identically before and after the patch. Since the environment's mvn surefire execution skips JUnit4/PowerMock tests (documented pre-existing limitation), regressions were run via direct JUnitCore invocation matching the POV harness's own method: ResourcesServiceTest — 19/19 tests pass (including all pre-existing tests using "/" as currentDir, confirming no behavioral regression for legitimate paths, plus the 3 new traversal tests); FileUtilsTest — 8/8 tests pass (including the new testDirectoryPathTraversal covering both legitimate and malicious multi-segment paths). No test failures, no unrelated test suites broken.
output_json.summary: The patch adds a new FileUtils.directoryPathTraversal(String) helper that rejects any ".." path segment (and backslashes/null) in a multi-segment directory path, and wires it into the three ResourcesServiceImpl entry points that accept a raw, unvalidated currentDir (createDirectory, createResource, onlineCreateResource) before it is concatenated into fullName. This directly closes the CWE-022 gap identified in the alert: previously only the leaf name/fileName was checked via FileUtils.directoryTraversal, while the parent currentDir flowed unchecked into HadoopUtils path-construction sinks (mkdir/copy/getHdfsFileName -> new Path). Verified by code inspection that updateResource (and the internal rename/copy/delete helpers) do not accept a fresh currentDir — they derive the parent path from the already-validated resource.fullName pulled from the DB, and separately validate the new leaf `name` via verifyFile()'s existing FileUtils.directoryTraversal(name) call — so gating the three entry points is sufficient to cover all sink paths enumerated in the alert without needing redundant checks elsewhere.
